01About

From electrical engineering to autonomous machines.

Yukesh is a final-year Electrical and Electronics Engineering student at KSR College of Engineering, Namakkal, Tamil Nadu, building toward a career as a Robotics Engineer.

His work sits at the intersection of hardware and intelligence — combining embedded systems, computer vision, and machine learning to build machines that sense, decide, and act. Projects range from PID-controlled line-following robots to an AI-driven battery management system trained on real sensor data, to a ROS 2 platform for autonomous mobile robot control.

Beyond coursework, he designs PCBs in Altium and KiCad, prototypes on ESP32 and Arduino, and is currently developing Robot-as-a-Service — a concept for bringing affordable, AI-guided robotic automation to small and medium manufacturers.

AI / ML · EMBEDDED

AI-Based Predictive Battery Management System

[ Add project photo / chart screenshot ]

An intelligent BMS combining battery sensing, embedded hardware, and machine learning for predictive maintenance. Trained on a dataset of ~11,000 entries (voltage, current, temperature, SOC, SOH, cycle count) to predict remaining useful life and classify fault status, reaching an R² of 0.918.

ESP32Python / MLPredictive MaintenanceVoltage · Current · Temp Sensors
INNOVATION · HACKATHON

Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) — VLA + LiDAR Safety

Problem: Small and medium manufacturers often lack access to affordable, easily deployable, and safe robotic automation systems.

Approach: A concept developed for MSME Hackathon 6.0 combining vision-language-action (VLA) reasoning with intelligent safety measures. It integrates LiDAR-based safety zones that detect nearby people to monitor the workspace continuously.

Result/Status: Successfully prototyped the core safety logic, allowing the robotic system to stop or reposition automatically when humans enter restricted zones, improving collaborative safety in industrial settings.

VLALiDARComputer VisionIndustrial Automation
Engineering projects

ESP32 PID Line-Following Robot

A robot that continuously detects a line and adjusts motor speeds using PID feedback control, built with ESP32, sensors, and real-time control logic.

Smart Solar Panel with Edge AI

Renewable-energy monitoring combined with on-device prediction using TensorFlow Lite on ESP32, moving inference to the edge for faster decisions.

IoT RFID Attendance System

An ESP32 + MFRC522 attendance system with OLED feedback and automatic logging to Google Sheets over Wi-Fi.
